clue.text: Given 11 bids, unusually, for special edition

indicators.note: done unusually, the letters of these words are set out in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, a passionate lover

explanation.surface: Someone offers bids for a special edition of a book, unusually generous ones.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' stands for the answer to that clue, ADORER; 'unusually' rearranges GIVEN, ADORER and BIDS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened text of a book is a particular, special form of its publication.

clue.text: Fawned, as did the young Kennedy!

definitions.meaning: to fawn is to behave obsequiously, bowing and scraping before someone
Nigel Kennedy, the violinist, drew a bow and scraped strings as a young prodigy

explanation.surface: A member of the Kennedy family is pictured as a youthful flatterer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kennedy is not the political family but Nigel Kennedy, the English violinist; a violinist bows and scrapes literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for obsequious grovelling also describes literally playing a violin with a bow.

clue.text: Victor downed whiskey outside The Bull

indicators.note: downed here means knocked out, so the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a victor is a winner
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A winning drinker knocks back a whisky outside a pub called The Bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downed' looks like drinking but signals taking W out. On a dartboard or archery target, the inner is the ring just outside the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target the ring immediately surrounding the central bullseye is called by this name.

clue.text: Contents of the stomach reportedly poisoned Wakeman

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is to be heard spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Rick Wakeman, keyboard player of the band Yes, poisoned with gas would be 'gassed Rick'

explanation.surface: A report claims Wakeman was poisoned, judging by what was found in his stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what belongs to the stomach, as in its digestive juices.

clue.text: Do you change colour?

definitions.meaning: an old or dialect contraction of 'do ye', said as one syllable
to colour cloth or hair with a pigment

explanation.surface: A question asking whether someone ever blushes or changes hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic d'ye contracts 'do ye'; colouring fabric with pigment is the second sense.

clue.text: One may be seen at breakfast, turning puce having eaten a horse!

definitions.text: One may be seen at breakfast

indicators.note: turning means the assembled letters are read in the opposite direction
having eaten means the colour word takes the horse inside it

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, GG

explanation.surface: Someone at breakfast turns puce after claiming to be so hungry they could eat a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a horse' is not a literal meal: gee-gee is nursery language for a horse, and the colour word swallows it before the whole is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A small holder for a boiled egg is a familiar item on the breakfast table.

clue.text: Like the general's plan to move 4 around the flanks

indicators.note: with 'around', move says the letters are shifted about into a new order
with 'move', around says the letters are shuffled about

parts.note: the answer to 4 down, relating to the stomach

indicators.note: the flanks of a word are its two outside letters

explanation.surface: A general plans to move a fourth unit around the enemy's flanks.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' stands for GASTRIC; 'the flanks' gives TE, the outer letters of 'the', and 'move ... around' rearranges all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A general's plan is a military strategy, and the adjective describes anything of that kind.

clue.text: Veteran priest spins no.1 German gospel song

parts.note: a veteran is an old-timer
Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: spins means the letters are turned round to run backwards

parts.note: no.1 written out is NO with 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A veteran priest gives his top German gospel song a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spins' reverses NOIG to give GION.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a well-known American gospel hymn, a song from the revivalist tradition.

clue.text: He, 21, gave leaders of ocean-going whaler Essex nourishment

definitions.text: He, 21, gave leaders of ocean-going whaler Essex nourishment

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their opening letters, read in order

explanation.surface: A grim fact from the 1820 sinking of the whaleship Essex, where a cabin boy was eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Owen Coffin was the young crewman of the Essex, the whaler sunk by a sperm whale, who drew lots and was eaten by his starving shipmates.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue tells the story of the castaway eaten by survivors of the doomed whaling ship.

clue.text: Fearful European girls hide when Rudolph's on the pull!

indicators.note: fearful girls are in a state, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Frightened European girls hide while a lothario called Rudolph is out on the pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the pull' is British slang for seeking a romantic partner; here Rudolph the reindeer is literally pulling Santa's transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph the reindeer pulls Santa's snow vehicle, so his pulling makes a festive outing.

clue.text: Passionate lover in sombrero, dad's back!

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A romantic in a Mexican hat announces that father has returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's hidden-word step lacked its indicator; 'in' signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who worships another ardently is a devoted, passionate admirer.

clue.text: Rowan, Pompeii's unexpected visitor

definitions.meaning: the rowan tree, with red berries, has this other common name
volcanic dust from Vesuvius fell on Pompeii without warning in AD 79

explanation.surface: Someone named Rowan turns up unannounced in ancient Pompeii.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan's alternative tree name doubles as the volcanic fallout that buried the Roman town.

clue.text: Located in Vermont (an American State)

indicators.note: located in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A statement locating something in Vermont, helpfully glossed as an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket makes 'an American State' look like a gloss on Vermont, but the definition names a different state.
explanation.definitionFit: A large western US state on the Canadian border, known as Big Sky Country.

clue.text: Getting sharper, new China works invested in engineering

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so these letters are put within the abbreviation

parts.note: ENG is the abbreviation for engineering

indicators.note: works means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Chinese factories have invested in engineering and are getting more competitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' reads as factories in the surface, but it is the signal to rearrange the new China letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Improving the clarity or quality of something, like a sharpened image, is a synonym.

clue.text: Theatres perform check over song playback

parts.note: to audit is to perform a check on accounts
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: playback says the word is played in reverse

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: Theatres check their performances by playing back a recorded song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playback' reverses AIR to give RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Latin-derived word for the seating part of a theatre, used for whole auditoriums or halls.

clue.text: Nash smuggled American out of Ethiopian region

indicators.note: with 'out of', smuggled says a letter is sneaked away from the word
with 'smuggled', out of says a letter is taken from the region's name

parts.note: the Ogaden is a region of eastern Ethiopia

explanation.surface: Someone called Nash smuggled an American out of a region of Ethiopia.
explanation.walkthrough: Nash looks like a surname for a smuggler; it is the American comic poet Ogden Nash.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogden Nash was the American writer of light verse, so his first name pairs with his surname.

clue.text: Single actor's confidence

definitions.meaning: a single record has a main track, its A-side
a remark spoken to the audience, which other characters supposedly cannot hear

explanation.surface: A lone actor shows great self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confidence' reads as self-belief but means a confided remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A record's lead track is its A-side; a stage remark shared with the audience alone is the second sense.

clue.text: Island where English Knut can't work

indicators.note: work means the letters are worked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The setter, Knut, names an island where he cannot get employment as an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own pseudonym, Knut, is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A Massachusetts island off Cape Cod, once a great whaling port.

clue.text: Hearts beat Queen of the South

parts.note: a tick is a beat, as of a clock
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A football result: Hearts beat Queen of the South, two Scottish clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts and Queen of the South are Scottish football clubs, so the surface reads as a match score.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the organ that beats in the chest, as a clock does.

clue.text: Here Alexandra plays dead, having served on board

parts.note: Crewe Alexandra is the football club of the English town of Crewe, so Crewe is where it plays

explanation.surface: A woman named Alexandra is acting dead after serving aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexandra looks like an actress; Crewe Alexandra is an English football club in the Cheshire town of Crewe.
explanation.definitionFit: To have staffed a ship or aircraft as a member of its company is to have done this.

clue.text: Held by spies, Tex half-heartedly agreed conditions

indicators.note: held by means the following letters sit inside the spy agency's initials

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency

indicators.note: the heart of the surname is a double T, and half of it is lost

parts.note: Tex Ritter was the American singing cowboy

explanation.surface: A Texan, held by spies, grudgingly accepts their terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Tex is not a Texan but Tex Ritter, the American singing cowboy; his surname loses one of its two central letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards or tests that all parties accept for judging something are its terms of assessment.

clue.text: Box leaves in a bit

indicators.note: in says the leaves go inside the piece of money

parts.note: a bit is an old word for a small coin, as in a threepenny bit
ff. abbreviates folios, the leaves of a book

explanation.surface: The box will be leaving in a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a bit' reads as 'soon'; the leaves (FF) are put in a coin. A threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang and everyday usage both call a burial casket a box.

clue.text: Managed soccer team without money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the team's letters surround the other piece

parts.note: FC stands for Football Club
ran means managed

explanation.surface: Someone managed a soccer team without any money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The former currency of France and the current one of Switzerland.

clue.text: One in school wheels pram around

indicators.note: around says the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A parent at school wheels a baby's pram around the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is the collective noun for a group of whales, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales gather in a school, so a large toothed whale is a member of one.

clue.text: See 12
Greedy Bill gobbles half a dozen

indicators.note: gobbles means swallows, so the word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, as a bill posted up
six is VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A greedy man called Bill gobbles six of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen or eager to the point of hunger, a near synonym of covetous.

clue.text: Mixed ward? These conditions are fit for the King!

indicators.note: the run of words is fitted to contain the letters, so they lie concealed across them

explanation.surface: A patient grumbles about a mixed hospital ward, insisting its conditions are fit for a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The ward and the hospital complaint are scenery; the letters run from the end of Mixed across ward and These into conditions. The king meant is the Plantagenet monarch deposed in 1327.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a medieval English monarch, Edward of Caernarfon, so he is an example of a sovereign.
